brief: A stone balance with two pans at the foot of a spiral stair; Dādī laying a palm-leaf verse on one pan and small stone grains on the other; Vṛttikā drifting past; Śuka reading the pans; Lubdhaka at a distance, taking notes.

A round stone vault at the foot of a spiral stair; a small ink-dark spirit tangled in a long cord of tiny knotted letters, knots at every joint; a carved verse on the wall with no gaps between words; Dādī kneeling beside the spirit; Śuka on the carved ledge reading; at the top of the stair, a tall figure in a dark coat in silhouette.

तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्य स्विद्धनम्
brief: The round vault wall covered in carved verses, each with small notes in faded ink all round it; Śuka on a ledge reading the notes round one verse aloud; Dādī beside him following with a finger; the small spirit Ślokikā with her cord slack on her lap, listening; warm lamplight.

The fourteenth statue with a long carved line running across her stone base; Dādī taking the chisel from the statue's hand and marking gaps between words; Lubdhaka's foreman standing back with his arms folded; Śuka reading over her shoulder.
